announcements.title: 37th Community Thanksgiving Meal
announcements.body: Join us on Thanksgiving morning, Thursday, November 26, as we prepare and deliver 750 Thanksgiving meals to those who need them throughout Alcorn County. This is a HUGE project and can only be accomplished with the help of many. It is a great opportunity for the members of FPC to be disciples by “living and loving like Jesus.”

announcements.title: Samaritan’s Purse Shoeboxes
announcements.body: Collection boxes are available in the children’s wing and the side entrance by the church office. You can participate by shopping and collecting items, or by donating monetarily — each shoebox costs $10 to ship. Items needed: small composition notebooks, pencils, small cars/trucks, puzzles, jump ropes, hair bows/barrettes/brushes/combs, underwear in larger sizes, and small stuffed animals. No liquids, candy, or food!

items.title: Call to Meditation
items.text: “The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.”

lines.text: Praise the Lord, O my soul, all my inmost being, praise his holy name!
Praise the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits,
Praise the Lord, O you his angels, you mighty ones who do his bidding, who obey his word.
Praise the Lord, all his heavenly hosts, you his servants who do his will!
Praise the Lord, all his works everywhere in his dominion.
Praise the Lord, O my soul!

items.title: Prayer of Invocation & The Lord’s Prayer
items.text: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy Kingdom come, thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.

lines.text: I prayed to the Lord my God and made confession, saying, “O Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments,
We have sinned and done wrong and acted wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from your commandments and rules.

To you, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us open shame, as at this day, to the men of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those who are near and those who are far away, in all the lands to which you have driven them, because of the treachery that they have committed against you.

To us, O Lord, belongs open shame, to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against you. To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him and have not obeyed the voice of the Lord our God by walking in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.

And now, O Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and have made a name for yourself, as at this day, we have sinned, we have done wickedly. Now therefore, O our God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to his pleas for mercy, and for your own sake, O Lord, make your face to shine upon your sanctuary, which is desolate.

O my God, incline your ear and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations, and the city that is called by your name. For we do not present our pleas before you because of our righteousness, but because of your great mercy.
O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive. O Lord, pay attention and act. Delay not, for your own sake, O my God, because your city and your people are called by your name.
Lord, we have sinned against you, yet you are merciful and forgiving. Hear us as we confess our sins, and restore us according to your steadfast love.

items.title: Corporate Prayer of Confession
items.text: Holy and gracious Father, You are righteous in all Your ways, yet we have sinned against You in thought, word, and deed. We have turned from Your commands, neglected Your Word, and loved our own ways more than Yours. We confess that we have not loved You with our whole hearts or loved our neighbors as ourselves. Forgive us, O Lord, not because of our righteousness, but according to Your great mercy. Restore us by Your grace, renew our hearts, and make us faithful to Your calling, that Your name might be honored among Your people.

items.text: Praise God, from whom all blessings flow; Praise Him, all creatures here below; Praise Him above, ye heavenly host; Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Amen.

The grass withers, the flower fades, but the Word of our God will stand forever. Amen.

notes.label: Prelude
notes.text: The prelude provides a quiet moment to prepare for worship. As the music begins, we are encouraged to calm our hearts, focus our minds, and enter reverently into God’s presence.

notes.label: O Worship the King
notes.text: This beautiful hymn, written by Sir Robert Grant, a British politician and hymn writer, was published in 1833. Inspired by Psalm 104, the hymn celebrates God’s majesty, power, and steadfast love. As we worship our great and holy King, we are reminded of our dependence upon His grace, leading us to confess our sins and trust in His covenant mercy.

notes.label: Invocation
notes.text: The word “invocation” suggests that the congregation calls upon God, yet this must not be misunderstood to mean that we bring God into our presence or that His nearness depends on our request. The Lord is already present with His people before our worship begins. To “invoke” is to call upon or earnestly seek. So, we lift our voices to God, asking Him to draw near and enable us to worship Him rightly for His character and mighty works.

notes.label: Call to Confession
notes.text: In Daniel 9, we hear a humble confession of God’s people, acknowledging His righteousness, their sin, and their need for mercy. As we read responsively, we join in this prayer of repentance, remembering that our hope rests not in our own righteousness, but in God’s steadfast covenant love and forgiveness.

notes.label: FPC Missions
notes.text: FPC currently provides prayer and financial support to over 50 international and domestic missionaries, along with 2 international ministry organizations and 6 local ministries. We want to introduce the congregation to several of these missionaries every month, so you can get to know them and pray specifically for them.

notes.label: Children’s Church
notes.text: Children ages 4 up to 4th grade are invited to come forward and exit out the side door for Children’s Church. Following the worship service, they may be picked up in the Fellowship Hall.

notes.label: Benediction
notes.text: God’s people are blessed by the Lord and sent forth into the world, bearing with them the hope and peace of the Gospel. This should remind us that God doesn’t just meet with us when we gather, but He goes with us as we scatter. As we continue our worship, we do so as people sent to our community for reconciliation, bearing witness to the good news of the gospel.

sermon.title: Spiritual Renewal: When God Begins to Work
intro: Welcome back to the story of God’s restoration. In the book of Ezra we saw a temple rebuilt and a community rooted again in the Word of God. We are going to keep going in the story and get into the Book of Nehemiah — in the Jewish Bible, Ezra and Nehemiah are one book. As we open the Book of Nehemiah, we discover that a beautiful house of worship is not enough if the city around it lies in ruins and the people inside are living in fear. Nehemiah takes us from the quiet halls of a Persian palace in Babylon to the rubble of a broken Jerusalem, shifting our focus from architectural reconstruction to a deep, messy, and urgent spiritual renewal.

The temple had been rebuilt, but Jerusalem’s walls still lay in ruins. God’s people had returned to the land, but they remained vulnerable and exposed. There had been real restoration, but there was still work to be done.

As we look at the first chapter of Nehemiah we see how God begins His work of restoration: by awakening His people to the brokenness around them and drawing them to Himself in prayer. Nehemiah 1 shows us where and how that work begins.

points.heading: II. God Draws His People to Himself
points.quote: Daniel 9:18 — “For we do not present our pleas before you because of our righteousness, but because of your great mercy.”
